newsitem.title: JAPAN: NTT says BT joint bid first step in int'l strategy.
newsitem.headline: NTT says BT joint bid first step in int'l strategy.

text.p: Japanese telecoms giant NTT Corp said on Friday that its joint bid with British Telecom for a phone licence in Singapore is the first step in its strategy to seek different partners for various projects and regions.

Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp, which has stressed its "multi-directional" approach in deals with global carriers, said its joining of hands with British Telecommunications Plc is not a prelude to a full tie-up.

"We have made clear that NTT would not tie up with any specific international consortium," a NTT spokesman said, adding that there is no possibility that the alliance will develop into its full membership in Concert, a global venture between BT and MCI Inc of the United States.
Rumours have been swirling over the past couple of months about which foreign carrier would be successful in courting NTT to gain a foothold in the lucrative Japanese communications market.
BT has so far been seen as the front-runner in the race and has been openly seeking NTT's membership in Concert.
For the Singapore project, NTT and BT have joined a consortium to bid for the island-state's second basic telecommunications services licence.
The NTT spokesman said this is the first time that NTT has formed a partnership with BT.
The other members of the consortium include Singapore Technologies Telemedia and Singapore Power.
After a feasibility study, NTT, BT and the two Singapore companies will bid for the tender scheduled around January 1998, he said. The licence will be awarded June 1998.
The Singapore government had earlier said it would allow at least one and possibly two new operators to operate fixed line telephone services.
Currently, Singapore Telecom has a monopoly in providing fixed line services.
NTT already operates in the Philippines, Indonesia and Thailand, and has plans underway in India.
